name: Upper Darby, Pennsylvania

rent.notes: Delaware County inner-ring suburb; ~20% below Philadelphia city for comparable 2BR. Older twin homes and apartments near the 69th Street Transportation Center. Water, sewer, and trash are separate utility bills.

sources.title: Zumper — Average Rent in Upper Darby, PA ($1,389 2BR avg)
RentCafe — Average Rent in Upper Darby, PA ($1,379 2BR avg)

groceries.notes: 2 adults + pet food. Diverse grocery scene (H Mart, international markets) keeps costs slightly below city average.

gas.notes: PECO / Philadelphia Gas region. Primary heating.

utilities.taxes: Pennsylvania exempts residential utilities from sales tax.
utilities.notes: Electricity, gas, water, sewage, trash. Internet is in entertainment.

healthcare.notes: Medicare Part B + Medigap Plan G (x2) + Part D (x2) + dental/vision. Same metro baseline as Philadelphia. NOTE: Crozer-Chester Medical Center and Taylor Hospital closed May 2025; Delaware County retains only Riddle (Media) and Mercy Fitzgerald (Darby, ~2 mi). Upper Darby is well-positioned regardless — Lankenau Medical Center ~4 mi and Penn Presbyterian reachable via the El.

sources.title: WHYY — Delaware County Crozer Health closure, longer ambulance rides

petCare.notes: Vet visits, vaccinations, flea/tick, pet insurance.

petDaycare.notes: Doggy daycare 2 days/week, large-breed rate. Suburban pricing slightly below Center City.

transportation.notes: 69th Street Transportation Center: SEPTA Market-Frankford Line terminus + trolleys + Norristown High Speed Line. Direct rail to Center City; car optional.

entertainment.notes: Incl cable+1Gig internet, streaming, dining out.

phoneCell.notes: T-Mobile 55+ Essentials. 2 phones, all taxes included.

buffer.notes: Monthly safety buffer for unexpected expenses.

medicalOOP.notes: Specialist visits, labs, and out-of-pocket shares after Medicare. Same metro provider network as Philadelphia.

medicine.notes: Monthly prescription medication costs for household.

taxes.notes: Estimated monthly income tax on $72,000/yr household income. PA flat 3.07% with SS/retirement exempt; no Philadelphia city wage tax outside the city (a 1% local EIT applies to earned income only, not retirement). Excludes sales/property tax.

healthcarePreMedicare.notes: ACA silver benchmark for a 2-adult household, both age ~60, before subsidies (county-level estimate, Delaware County). Shares Pennsylvania's Philadelphia-region rating area with Philadelphia, so the benchmark matches the Philadelphia base. Estimated +/-15% vs a healthcare.gov quote. Verify a specific ZIP on Pennie (pennie.com). Accessed 2026-07-29.

stateIncomeTax.exemptions: SS and all retirement income exempt from PA tax. Local Earned Income Tax (~1%) applies to earned income only, not retirement income. No Philadelphia city wage tax outside the city.

salesTax.notes: 6% state; Delaware County has no local sales-tax add-on (unlike Philadelphia's 8%).

propertyTax.notes: Not modeled for renters; Delaware County effective property-tax rates are among the higher in the metro and are reflected in rents.

taxes.notes: PA exempts all retirement income from state tax. Lower combined sales tax than Philadelphia (6% vs 8%) and no city wage tax.

acaMarketplace.notes: Pennie (PA state marketplace). Delaware County shares the Philadelphia-region rating area; benchmark matches the Philadelphia base.
acaMarketplace.disclaimer: Estimated +/-15% vs a healthcare.gov/Pennie quote. Verify a specific ZIP on pennie.com. Accessed 2026-07-29.

pros: Direct SEPTA rail to Center City from the 69th Street hub
No Philadelphia city wage tax; lower 6% sales tax
PA exempts SS and retirement income from state tax
Diverse, walkable inner-ring suburb with strong transit
cons: Higher Delaware County property taxes (baked into rents)

cons.text: Safety & crime: see cited reports for current figures by city and country
